notes:
Account summary: Crownhall Product Labs (VP Product: Maya Ortiz) building an embedded product analytics assistant and in-app summarization. They are a mid-market SaaS buyer evaluating Redwood Hosted API first (6-week POC) with the intent to move to Dedicated capacity if latency/price targets are met. Conversation history: demo 2026-02-28, technical deep-dive 2026-03-02, security kickoff 2026-03-05.

Key requirements and constraints:
- Workloads: chat support agent (multi-turn), document search/embedding indexing, reranking for prioritized hits, end-user summarization in product UI.
- Latency SLOs: p99 <= 150ms for chat generation for short prompts; embeddings throughput target 30 qps for nightly bulk; reranking latency target <= 80ms for small top-K.
- Cost sensitivity: high — finance wants modeled unit economics showing per-session cost <= $0.03 on average and path to 30-50% savings after optimizations.
- Deployment plan: start on Redwood Hosted API for speed of integration, then Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for predictable unit costs and VPC network requirements.
- Security: require SSO/SAML, SOC2 compliance evidence, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, KMS integration for key management, potential EU data residency for a subset of customers.

POC & technical notes:
- Demo feedback: liked streaming + function-calling for in-product actions. Concerned about token costs at scale.
- Baseline tests (Redwood SE ran synthetic baseline): 13B open model at default FP16 gave p95~90ms on hosted with batching disabled; estimated token cost higher than target.
- POC scope: 6-week window. Week 1-2 integration + sample workloads. Week 3 cost-workshop with engineering + finance. Weeks 4-5 live A/B with control group. Week 6 decision & pricing negotiation.
- Cost optimization workshop goals: demonstrate batching (dynamic batching profiles), prefix/KV caching for repeated context, recommended quantization profiles (8-bit and 4-bit tradeoffs), and show unit economics models for Hosted vs Dedicated. Target: show >=35% reduction through batching+caching+quantization for their mix.

Quotes / snippets from calls:
- "We want to avoid a surprise bill — need deterministic unit costs and a clear migration path." — Maya Ortiz (VP Product).
- "If Dedicated gets us to predictable per-session cost, we'll buy reserved capacity." — CTO Alex Ruiz.

Risks / open questions:
- Security review timeline: Legal wants full SOC2 + security FAQ answered before mid-April.
- Fallback behavior: need documented deterministic fallback chain (hosted -> dedicated variants) and how quality changes are communicated to product.
- Model governance: who owns prompt/quality evals internally; they want Redwood Optimize integration for automated regression alerts.

Next steps (short):
- Send technical prep pack (sample batching configs, quantization tradeoff doc) by 2026-03-12 (assigned to Riley).
- Cost-optimization workshop scheduled 2026-03-18 (invite sent). Attendees: Maya Ortiz, Alex Ruiz, Eng lead Priya Sinha, Finance lead Tomas Vega, Redwood AE Avery Chen, SE Riley Morgan.
- Security pack request placed — expect security review slots week of 2026-03-22.

Stated business outcome: Reduce inference unit cost to enable 3x scale of active users without linear cost growth; convert to Dedicated reserved capacity within 2 quarters if POC validates economics.
